claims.text: Shifting the d-band center of a transition-metal catalyst closer to the Fermi level enhances catalytic activity.
Shifting the d-band center closer to the Fermi level enhances catalytic selectivity.
The activity and selectivity enhancement occurs because the d-band shift optimizes binding strength with reaction intermediates.
Alloying can shift the d-band center relative to the Fermi level.
A shift in the d-band center alters the adsorption strength of reactants and intermediates.
Moving the d-band center closer to the Fermi level optimizes bond formation.
Moving the d-band center closer to the Fermi level lowers activation barriers.
Optimized bonding and lower activation barriers increase turnover frequency.
Optimized bonding and lower activation barriers enhance selectivity.
Catalysts whose d-band centers are shifted closer to the Fermi level will have higher activity than an unmodified pure-metal baseline under the same reaction conditions.
Catalysts whose d-band centers are shifted closer to the Fermi level may have improved selectivity relative to an unmodified baseline.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold when electronic structure largely governs adsorption.
The proposed relationship may fail when strong metal-support interactions or other factors dominate catalytic behavior.
The optimal d-band shift and its quantitative effect may vary with catalyst composition and reaction conditions.
XPS or UPS can be used to measure d-band-center positions relative to the Fermi level.
